items.name: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini apps
items.summary: The consumer apps send what you type straight to their own servers and have no setting to change that, so no proxy, this one included, can sit in front of them. Use the same models privately through a chat app you control.
steps: Open the built-in playground at `{ANTHROPIC_BASE}/#/playground` to chat with any configured model through the gateway.
Or run Open WebUI or LibreChat (below): a ChatGPT-style app where every message passes through the gateway.
Configure the provider once on the gateway (`harpo init --provider openai`, `anthropic`, `gemini` or `openrouter`).

notes.text: A browser extension that checks what you paste into chatgpt.com or claude.ai against this gateway is on the roadmap. Until then, the apps above are the private route.

items.name: Built-in playground
items.summary: This console. See what a prompt turns into before it leaves, then send it to any configured model and read the reply.
steps: Open `{ANTHROPIC_BASE}/#/playground`.
Type or pick a sample. The right pane is exactly what the provider receives.
Choose a model and press Send. Replies come back with placeholders: redaction is one-way.

items.name: Open WebUI
items.summary: A self-hosted, ChatGPT-style interface. Point its OpenAI connection at the gateway and every chat is sanitized first.

snippets.label: Docker
snippets.code:
docker run -d --name open-webui -p 3000:8080 \
  -e OPENAI_API_BASE_URL={OPENAI_BASE} \
  -e OPENAI_API_KEY={KEY} \
  -e ENABLE_OLLAMA_API=false \
  -v open-webui:/app/backend/data \
  ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:main

snippets.label: Compose profile
snippets.code:
# from this repository: gateway + Open WebUI, already wired together
docker compose --profile chat up -d
open http://localhost:3000

notes.text: Running it in Docker? Inside a container `localhost` is the container itself: use `http://host.docker.internal:8080/v1` (Docker Desktop) or the gateway's service name, or use `docker compose --profile chat up`, which wires Open WebUI to the gateway for you.

items.name: LibreChat
items.summary: A multi-provider chat app. Add the gateway as a custom endpoint; models are listed from the gateway's /v1/models.

snippets.label: librechat.yaml
snippets.code:
endpoints:
  custom:
    - name: "Harpo"
      apiKey: "${HARPO_KEY}"
      baseURL: "{OPENAI_BASE}"
      models:
        default: ["{MODEL}"]
        fetch: true
      titleConvo: true
      titleModel: "current_model"

notes.text: Running it in Docker? Inside a container `localhost` is the container itself: use `http://host.docker.internal:8080/v1` (Docker Desktop) or the gateway's service name, or use `docker compose --profile chat up`, which wires Open WebUI to the gateway for you.

Base URL: `{OPENAI_BASE}` · API key: `{KEY}` · Model: `{MODEL}`.

items.name: Claude Code
items.summary: Anthropic's coding agent reads ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL. Your code, logs and secrets are sanitized before they reach the model.

snippets.label: Shell

notes.text: Through OpenRouter: configure the `openrouter-messages` upstream (the boot scripts do it), keep `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL={ANTHROPIC_BASE}`, and set `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL` (and the Opus and Haiku variants) to OpenRouter model names such as `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5`.

Claude Code adopts new API fields early. If a request is refused with `Not inspected by the gateway`, the error names the field path: set `policy.unknown_fields: pass` to scan such fields as text, and open an issue so the adapter can declare it.
Screenshots you paste are images: blocked by default (`policy.unsupported_content`). Keys and passwords in files it reads arrive as `[SECRET_1]`: they are always redacted, and the request goes on.

items.name: OpenAI Codex CLI
items.summary: Add the gateway as a model provider in ~/.codex/config.toml, using the Chat Completions wire API.

snippets.label: config.toml
snippets.code:
model = "{MODEL}"
model_provider = "harpo"

[model_providers.harpo]
name = "Harpo"
base_url = "{OPENAI_BASE}"
env_key = "HARPO_API_KEY"
wire_api = "chat"

snippets.label: Shell
snippets.code:
export HARPO_API_KEY={KEY}
codex

notes.text: The gateway proxies Chat Completions and Anthropic Messages; the OpenAI Responses API is on the roadmap, hence `wire_api = "chat"`.

items.name: Cursor
items.summary: Cursor can override the OpenAI base URL, but it calls custom endpoints from its own servers.
steps: Settings → Models → OpenAI API key: `{KEY}`; enable **Override OpenAI Base URL**.
The URL must be reachable from the internet (HTTPS), not localhost.

notes.text: Cursor's servers handle your prompt before it reaches the gateway, so the gateway cannot protect it from Cursor. Prefer Continue, Cline or Claude Code, which connect from your machine.

items.name: OpenAI SDK for Python
items.summary: Set base_url, or set OPENAI_BASE_URL and change no code.

snippets.label: Python
snippets.code:
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="{OPENAI_BASE}", api_key="{KEY}")
reply = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="{MODEL}",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Email jane.doe@acme.com about her refund"}],
)
print(reply.choices[0].message.content)

snippets.label: Environment
snippets.code:
export OPENAI_BASE_URL={OPENAI_BASE}
export OPENAI_API_KEY={KEY}   # the gateway key; your provider key stays on the gateway

items.name: Anthropic SDK for Python
items.summary: Messages, streaming and token counting all go through the gateway.

snippets.label: Python
snippets.code:
from anthropic import Anthropic

client = Anthropic(base_url="{ANTHROPIC_BASE}", api_key="{KEY}")
message = client.messages.create(
    model="{CLAUDE_MODEL}",
    max_tokens=1024,
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Email jane.doe@acme.com about her refund"}],
)
print(message.content[0].text)

snippets.label: Environment
snippets.code:
export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL={ANTHROPIC_BASE}
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY={KEY}

items.name: curl and plain HTTP
items.summary: Any language with an HTTP client: the request shape is OpenAI's or Anthropic's.

snippets.label: OpenAI style
snippets.code:
curl {OPENAI_BASE}/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer {KEY}" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "{MODEL}", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Email jane.doe@acme.com"}]}'

snippets.label: Anthropic style
snippets.code:
curl {ANTHROPIC_BASE}/v1/messages \
  -H "x-api-key: {KEY}" -H "anthropic-version: 2023-06-01" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "{CLAUDE_MODEL}", "max_tokens": 256, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Email jane.doe@acme.com"}]}'

snippets.label: Scan only
snippets.code:
curl {ANTHROPIC_BASE}/v1/scan -H "Authorization: Bearer {KEY}" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"text": "Email jane.doe@acme.com, card 4111 1111 1111 1111"}'

items.name: LangChain
items.summary: ChatOpenAI and ChatAnthropic both take a base URL.

snippets.label: Python
snippets.code:
from langchain_anthropic import ChatAnthropic
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI

gpt = ChatOpenAI(base_url="{OPENAI_BASE}", api_key="{KEY}", model="{MODEL}")
claude = ChatAnthropic(base_url="{ANTHROPIC_BASE}", api_key="{KEY}", model="{CLAUDE_MODEL}")
print(gpt.invoke("Email jane.doe@acme.com about her refund").content)

items.name: OpenAI Agents SDK
items.summary: Give the SDK a client pointed at the gateway, use Chat Completions, and turn off tracing.

snippets.label: Python
snippets.code:
from openai import AsyncOpenAI
from agents import Agent, Runner, set_default_openai_api, set_default_openai_client, set_tracing_disabled

set_default_openai_client(AsyncOpenAI(base_url="{OPENAI_BASE}", api_key="{KEY}"))
set_default_openai_api("chat_completions")  # the gateway proxies Chat Completions
set_tracing_disabled(True)  # traces would go to OpenAI directly, unredacted

agent = Agent(name="Support", instructions="Be brief.", model="{MODEL}")
print(Runner.run_sync(agent, "Email jane.doe@acme.com about her refund").final_output)

notes.text: Tracing uploads full traces to OpenAI outside the gateway. Keep it disabled, or send traces to a processor you host.

items.name: OpenRouter
items.summary: Hundreds of models behind one key, through both the OpenAI and the Anthropic API. The gateway enforces OpenRouter's privacy routing on every request: only providers that do not store prompts, optionally zero-data-retention endpoints only.
steps: Start with `boot.cmd` (Windows) or `./boot.sh` and choose `openrouter`, or run `harpo init --provider openrouter`. Both configure the OpenAI-style API and the Anthropic-style API that Claude Code uses.
Point clients at the gateway as usual. OpenRouter-native clients and SDKs can use `{ANTHROPIC_BASE}/api/v1`.
Use OpenRouter's model names (`anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5`). `GET /v1/models` lists the OpenRouter models your config allows.

snippets.label: Config
snippets.code:
upstreams:
  - name: openrouter
    style: openai
    base_url: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1
    api_key_env: OPENROUTER_API_KEY
    models: ["anthropic/*", "openai/*", "google/*"]
    openrouter:
      data_collection: deny   # enforced: only providers that do not store prompts
      zdr: true               # optional: zero-data-retention endpoints only
  - name: openrouter-messages # the Anthropic-style API (Claude Code)
    style: anthropic
    base_url: https://openrouter.ai/api
    api_key_env: OPENROUTER_API_KEY
    models: ["*"]

snippets.label: Shell
snippets.code:
export OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-...
harpo serve --config config/harpo.yaml

snippets.label: Python
snippets.code:
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="{OPENAI_BASE}", api_key="{KEY}")
reply = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
    extra_body={"provider": {"sort": "price"}},  # data_collection is set by the gateway
)

notes.text: Clients can tighten routing (zdr, only, ignore) but never loosen it: a request asking for providers that store data is rewritten to `data_collection: deny`. Fallback lists (`models`, `fallbacks`) must name models this upstream allows; router plugins (auto-router, fusion) are accepted only when it allows any model.

The connection test on Providers & adapters uses OpenRouter's key endpoint and shows the key's remaining limit and spend: OpenRouter lists models to anyone, so a model listing proves nothing about the key.
OpenRouter's web search and server tools run at OpenRouter, on the sanitized request. Generated images and other attachments are refused (`policy.unsupported_content`).
